div.head: Cons Cn Inscr.
div.ab: Hic incipiunt leges Cnuti regis Anglorum, Danorum et Nororum, uiri iustissimi et probatissimi.
Incipiunt leges que uocantur leges Edwardi, quia cum diu essent dimisse, ipsas fecit reparare. Et de legibus regis Willelmi.
div.note: New row (October 2026): Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 618 (two independent readings of the page images, differences settled against the page); Liebermann’s heading: [Consiliatio Cnuti.]

note.seg: Inscr. roth Cb; den Anfang bis I 17 lässt fort Hk, wo vorangeht ECf.
Inscr. in red Cb; the beginning up to I 17 is omitted by Hk, where ECf. precedes
diese Inscr. benutzt bereits den ECf. 34, 3, ist also nicht original. Die Gleichsetzung von Eadwards Recht mit dem Cnuts wäre zu Heinrichs I. Zeit möglich; vgl. Hn 20, 3n
this Inscr. already uses ECf. 34, 3, and is therefore not original. The equating of Eadward's law with Cnut's would be possible in the time of Henry I; cf. Hn 20, 3n
damit meint Hr ECf., der in Hr auf Cons. Cn. folgt und ihm damit als Ein Werk gilt
by this Hr means ECf., which in Hr follows Cons. Cn. and is thus regarded as forming a single work with it
Dieses Lob ist vielleicht blosse Floskel; doch s. Gl Cnut 5
This praise is perhaps a mere flourish; but see Gl Cnut 5

div.ab: Here begin the laws of Cnut, king of the English, Danes and Norwegians, a most just and most approved man.
Here begin the laws which are called the laws of Edward, because, when they had long been neglected, he had them restored. And of the laws of King William.
